native_context: Service worker scope, lifecycle and private response storage
taxonomy_note: Planning compatibility lens only. Classify the final observed root cause independently; unsupported mappings stay unassigned.

controls.boundary: Service worker scope, lifecycle and private response storage — authoritative consumer
controls.source_trace: Inspect worker registration scope, controlled clients, fetch routing, cache keys and account/logout/update policy. Distinguish worker CacheStorage from intermediary HTTP caches.
controls.controlled_verification: Cache a private synthetic account-A response via the normal feature, then perform the declared logout/account-switch flow and request the same resource as B/offline. Observe the source and marker of the returned response. Separately trace untrusted control of worker script URL or registration scope only if the application exposes such a path.
controls.false_positive_discriminator: A worker being registered or private data being available offline to its rightful account is not itself a leak. Browser storage partitioning, scope and lifecycle prerequisites must match the tested context.
controls.remediation_acceptance: Bind private cache entries and lifecycle cleanup to the declared account policy; use trusted worker code/registration inputs. Retest intended offline behavior, logout/account switch and the evidenced update path.

coverage_unit: One primary investigative assertion for this technique; not exhaustive coverage. Expand only for genuinely distinct policy/effect assertions in the actual assessment.
